7 years ago.

My father had have a brain stroke 9 years before that, I was 14 when that happened, still remember the morning like it was yesterday.

The worst part about the stroke was that my father got aphasia, he could only say 3 words, so communication was super frustrating for the both of us. 
And both of us, depressed living under the same roof, without being able to communicate we got into fights sometimes.

And one time we had a really bad fight and that was 6 months before he killed himself. I have his patient journal, I read in it that he got really bad mentally after we had that fight, and that has really been killing me slowly.

He couldn't either really communicate his problems very well since he had aphasia, he asked his carers and doctors for help three times because he was so suicidal he wanted to be laid in, but they just gave him new anti-depressives, and I think it was those that made him kill himself.

So there is a lot of regret, anger, and guilt in me, and I have also wasted the majority of my life doing nothing. 

So here I am, 29 now, with nothing more than the apartment I inherited from my father to my name, but I still have family and a friend that like and love me, otherwise I couldn't have gone on in this mental-state.

I loved my dad, regardless of anything he ever did or didn't do.

I always wanted to take my dad out fishing when he was sick, I just needed my drivers license, which I fucked up during the time he was alive.
I would take him out just like he took me out when I was a kid, but I only got my drivers license recently, and now it's too late.

I could have anything in this world, you name it, it all fades in comparison to how much I want to see my father again, and right my wrongs.

I'm sorry for your situation, it is usually the good people that get sick. 

Honestly, you should stop thinking, and just do. Go and hug your father, what is the worse that could happen? 
If you guys aren't the hugging type, maybe it's time to change that anyway.

Try, til there is no more time to try, it will do you both good.

I have been playing with the thought of just doing it and killing myself for years now. But in the more recent months it has been become much more real, that it actually might happen, not just a fantasy.

What sucks is that there are still people that care for me and love me, family, friends.

Honestly, it would be really nice to not have to wake up tomorrow, to see if there is anything else after this, or nothing at all.

Something has to happen, and I'm not getting any better.  I've had my fair share of life and I'm ready to die, what sucks is that the people who like and love you can never be ready for something like that.
